title: CSRD & climate disclosure → procurement-linked evidence
floras_mechanism: For companies facing mandatory or investor-driven climate disclosure (CSRD, SEC climate rules, CDP, assurance expectations), Floras provides transaction-linked evidence: procurement and supplier activity that generates Floras, wallet allocation to verified projects, and certificates documenting impact. This supports auditable, activity-backed sustainability narratives — not generic marketing claims disconnected from business operations.
pain_signals: disclosure requirements demand auditable activity-backed evidence
sustainability claims feel disconnected from business operations
assurance or audit scrutiny on ESG narratives
procurement and Scope 3 data gaps weaken disclosure quality
investor pressure for measurable, traceable climate action
annual offset purchases lack link to operational activity
budget_source: ESG reporting and compliance budget; procurement program budget; assurance and disclosure budget
safe_claims: Floras links climate-designated value to business transactions, supporting activity-backed reporting
Certificates document which projects were supported and can complement disclosure workflows
Transaction-linked Floras can help connect procurement activity to funded climate impact
Floras supports evidence for sustainability narratives when aligned with actual purchasing activity
conditional_claims: If the company faces CSRD or SEC climate disclosure timelines, Floras can support procurement-linked evidence layers
If CDP or assurance is mentioned, transaction-linked certificates may strengthen activity-backed claims
If Scope 3 is a disclosure focus, supplier-embedded Floras can complement data collection narratives
avoid_claims: Floras satisfies CSRD, SEC, or CDP requirements by itself
Floras replaces assurance, audit, or formal disclosure filings
Floras eliminates the need for emissions inventory or supplier data

output_templates.one_liner: Give {company_name} transaction-linked climate evidence for disclosure — not disconnected offset slides.
output_templates.short_pitch: {company_name} faces rising disclosure and assurance expectations where generic sustainability language is no longer enough. Floras ties climate-designated value to qualifying business transactions — especially procurement and supplier activity — then routes that value through a wallet to verified projects with certificates. That gives sustainability and procurement teams activity-backed evidence to support CSRD, CDP, or investor-facing narratives without treating climate funding as a separate, untraceable annual purchase.

objections_and_responses.objection: We already have a disclosure platform and carbon accounting tool.
objections_and_responses.response: Floras complements measurement and reporting tools — it adds a transaction-linked funding and certificate layer connected to procurement activity, which accounting platforms typically do not provide on their own.

objections_and_responses.objection: Assurance providers will not accept this.
objections_and_responses.response: Position Floras as activity-linked evidence and documented project allocation with certificates, not as a substitute for assurance scope. Claims should stay within safe-claim boundaries and match what research supports.

objections_and_responses.objection: Regulation is a legal/compliance issue, not procurement.
objections_and_responses.response: Disclosure quality increasingly depends on Scope 3 and supplier activity — where procurement lives. Floras gives procurement and sustainability a shared, transaction-linked mechanism that supports the evidence investors and regulators expect behind the narrative.
